subject: English
question_text: What are the main features of the day?
guide_solution: The Independence Day is the biggest state festival. This day is celebrated every year in the country with great enthusiasm. It is a national holiday. On this day, all offices, educational institutions, shops and factories remain closed. This day begins with a 31 gun shot.
source: SSC English 1st-paper Sylhet Board-2019 (Made Easy BQ)

subject: English
question_text: Why do people from all walks of life go to the National Mausoleum according to the text?
guide_solution: On 26 March people of all classes go to the National Mausoleum at Savar to pay homage to the martyrs of Liberation War in 1971. They also remember the great struggle and sacrifice of the freedom fighters.
source: SSC English 1st-paper Sylhet Board-2019 (Made Easy BQ)

subject: English
question_text: What are the most spectacular events of the day?
guide_solution: The most spectacular events of the day are parade of defence forces at the National Parade Ground, various displays in National Stadium, sports meets and tournaments including boat race, etc.

subject: English
question_text: What kind of programmes are held other than the parade?
guide_solution: Other than the parade, various cultural programmes highlighting the heroic struggle and sacrifice in the liberation war, various displays, sports meets and tournaments, etc. are held on this day.

subject: English
question_text: Which leading organisations of our country organise cultural programmes on this day?
guide_solution: Bangla Academy, Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy and other socio-cultural organisations arrange cultural functions on the occasion of our Independence Day.

subject: English
question_text: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) is an organisation
stimulus: established for the promotion of mutual cooperation, friendship and development of the SAARC enlisted countries. It was Bangladesh that took the first initiative to form ,thisorganisation. SAARC started its journey through its first conference in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. At first there were seven developing nations under this organisation later - Afghanistan was included. The other- countries are .Bangladesh., Bhutan, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka. Bangladesh has been playing a significant role in SAARC from the beginning. It is trying to expand the trade between the member countries and to solve the regional conflicts and existing crisis between the neighbouring countries.
